proposals.before: In Taihe 4 (1204) Zhang Xingxin of the Hedong Surveillance Commission reported, "After the rotation law was abolished, clerk power gradually grew heavy; they seize as they please and the people dare not speak.
proposals.after: In Taihe 4 (1204) Zhang Xingxin, signatory for the Hedong Surveillance Commission, reported, "After the rotation law was abolished, clerk power gradually grew heavy; they seize as they please and the people dare not speak.
proposals.reason: Chinese 簽…事 marks an acting/signatory commission post; the idiomatic English drops that office nuance present in the literal.

proposals.before: In year 8 (1208), following Yang Yunyi's advice, surveillance clerks and scribes could not be locals; clerks from other circuits with special ministry recommendations took category exams, and successful candidates were appointed.
proposals.after: In year 8 (1208), following the advice of Yang Yunyi, acting for the Eastern Capital Surveillance Commission, document clerks and scribes were not to be natives of the circuit; clerks from other circuits specially recommended to the ministry took category exams, and those selected were appointed.
proposals.reason: Chinese names Yang with the full acting surveillance-commission title; the idiomatic line omits that office and softens 書吏書史.

proposals.before: Mixed-class bureaus included falconry, cooks, cart custodians, tent officers, armory guards, animal handlers, treasury officers, musicians, crossbowmen, and umbrella-bearers.
proposals.after: Mixed-class bureaus included falconry attendants, food-bureau cooks, fruit cooks, food-storehouse cart custodians, ceremonial-escort tent officers, armory spear-stockade officers, animal handlers, cash-and-silk treasury officers, banner-drum-flute-horn singers, crossbowmen, and umbrella-bearers.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic collapses distinct bureau posts (鷹坊子, 尚食局廚子, 果子廚子, 食庫車本把, 儀鸞典幄, 武庫槍寨, 錢帛庫官, 旗鼓笛角唱曲子人) into generic labels and omits several source-specific offices.

proposals.before: In Dading 29 senior attendants served three hundred months and ten-person chiefs ninety before leaving service.
proposals.after: In Dading 29 senior attendants served three hundred months and ten-person chiefs ninety months before leaving service.
proposals.reason: Chinese 九十月 explicitly measures months; idiomatic drops the unit after ninety and obscures the parallel with 三百月.

proposals.before: In Dading 6 yin heirs leaving company-commander terms took seventh-rank chief commander or chief captain, while others and fifty-household yin heirs took eighth-rank transit commissioner, patrol inspector, or deputy captain.
proposals.after: In Dading 6 yin heirs leaving company-commander terms took seventh-rank chief commander or chief captain, while others and fifty-household yin heirs took eighth-rank prefectural posts, chief patrol inspector, or deputy captain.
proposals.reason: 刺郡 means prefectural appointment as prefect, not a transit commissioner; 都巡檢 is chief patrol inspector.

proposals.before: In Dading 6, when company commanders' terms ended, those with yin privilege were noted for seventh-rank chief commander and chief captain; those without yin and fifty-household chiefs with yin were noted for eighth-rank transit commissioner, chief patrol inspector, and deputy captain.
proposals.after: In Dading 6, when company commanders' terms ended, those with yin privilege were noted for seventh-rank chief commander and chief captain; those without yin and fifty-household chiefs with yin were noted for eighth-rank prefectural posts, chief patrol inspector, and deputy captain.
proposals.reason: 刺郡 is prefectural appointment as prefect; translating it as transit commissioner is a clear office mistranslation.

proposals.before: In Zhenyuan 1 more than sixty physicians were dismissed.
proposals.after: In Zhenyuan 1 more than sixty persons were once dismissed.
proposals.reason: Chinese 六十餘人 means more than sixty persons; idiomatic invents physicians not stated in this sentence.

decisions.after: In Taihe 4 (1204), Zhang Xingxin, Assistant Commissioner in the Hedong Surveillance Commission, reported, "After the rotation law was abolished, clerk power gradually grew heavy; they seize as they please and the people dare not speak.
decisions.reason: The source gives Zhang's full office as 簽河東按察司事. 'Assistant Commissioner in the Hedong Surveillance Commission' preserves the subordinate commission post in natural English more clearly than the proposal's literal 'signatory.'

sourceWitness.excerpt: 簽河東按察司事張行信

decisions.after: In year 8 (1208), following the advice of Yang Yunyi, Assistant Commissioner in the Eastern Capital Surveillance Commission, document clerks and scribes were barred from serving in their home circuit; clerks from other circuits who were specially recommended to the ministry took category examinations, and successful candidates were appointed.
decisions.reason: The source identifies Yang by the office 僉東京按察司事 and expressly excludes 本路人. The revision restores both points while avoiding the proposal's awkward 'acting for' construction.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 僉東京按察司事楊雲翼言，書吏書史皆不用本路人

decisions.after: Mixed-class bureaus included falconry attendants; cooks for the Imperial Food Bureau and fruit kitchen; cart custodians for the provisions storehouse; ceremonial tent attendants; armory stockade guards; animal handlers; treasury officers; banner, drum, flute, and horn musicians and singers; crossbowmen; and umbrella-bearers.
decisions.reason: The existing sentence collapses several distinct posts into generic cooks, guards, and musicians. The revision preserves the source's occupational distinctions without reproducing the proposal's cumbersome compound labels.

decisions.reason: The source explicitly gives 九十月. Restoring 'months' after ninety removes an accidental unit omission and preserves the parallel with 三百月.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 長行三百月、十人長九十月出職

decisions.after: In Dading 6, when company commanders completed their terms, those with yin privilege were assigned to seventh-rank posts as chief commanders or captains. Those without yin privilege, and fifty-household chiefs with it, were assigned to eighth-rank prefectural posts or served as chief patrol inspectors or deputy captains.
decisions.reason: 刺郡 denotes prefectural appointments and cannot mean 'transit commissioner'; 都巡檢 is the chief patrol-inspector post. The revision also makes the two privilege classes and their possible assignments readable in English.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 注八品刺郡、都巡檢、副將

decisions.after: In Dading 6, when company commanders' terms ended, those with yin privilege were assigned to seventh-rank posts as chief commanders or captains; those without yin privilege, and fifty-household chiefs with it, were assigned to eighth-rank prefectural posts, or as chief patrol inspectors or deputy captains.
decisions.reason: The literal translation's 'transit commissioner' has no basis in 刺郡. The revision preserves the source's rank and appointment structure while rendering the listed prefectural and military offices directly.

decisions.reason: The preceding sentence supplies 太醫, 'imperial physicians,' as the continuing subject. English must make that ellipsis explicit, so 'more than sixty physicians' is accurate and the proposed generic 'persons' is less clear.
